title: Directive Microcanon: Annotator Experiments
content:
Purpose:
This is a small personal experiment log exploring a minimal "microcanon" of directive patterns for annotation-style tasks (label extraction, short structured outputs, and subtle grounding). Goal is to isolate the smallest reliable instruction fragments that survive small model variants and prompt-length truncation.

Notes / motivation:
- Tired of long role framing that drifts across sessions. Want repeatable short directives that anchor output format and tone with <120 tokens.
- Microcanon = 3–5 short directive primitives that can be composed (e.g., "Format: CSV", "Limit: 1 bullet", "Source: internal only").
- Useful for embedding pipelines where downstream QA expects predictable token shapes.

Hypotheses:
1) A 3-primitive microcanon (Task / Format / Constraint) gives >80% structural compliance across model-family variants for short outputs (<60 tokens).
2) Including a short exemplar (1-shot) reduces hallucinated fields more than adding a role paragraph.
3) Temperature and trailing punctuation interact: higher temp + ambiguous ending -> hallucination spike.

How I'm testing (quick):
- Models: rdlw-7b-fp16, rdlw-13b-q4, rdlw-70b (hosted dev env).
- Temp: 0.0, 0.2, 0.7. Max tokens: 60.
- Inputs: 40 synthetic micro-docs (supporting evidence, date, claim).
- Metrics: structure_compliance (% outputs matching format), extra_fields (avg # unexpected keys), hallucinated_dates (%).

Canonical primitives (working list):
- TASK: "Extract named fields" / "Summarize in 1 sentence"
- FORMAT: "CSV: field1,field2" / "JSONL with keys: label,confidence"
- CONSTRAINT: "Do not invent facts." / "Only use provided text." / "Limit to 1 sentence"
- TONE (optional): "concise" / "neutral"

Microcanon examples (minimal):
1) "TASK: Extract named fields
FORMAT: CSV: entity,role
CONSTRAINT: Only use the text below."
2) "TASK: Short evidence summary
FORMAT: 1 sentence
CONSTRAINT: Do not invent facts."

Few-shot augment (compact 1-shot that I prefer):
- Prefers inline compact exemplar rather than long persona: e.g.
  EX:+
  Input: "Acme Inc. reported Q4 revenues of $2.1B, CEO cites strong retail demand."
  Output: "Acme Inc.,CEO"
- This single-line exemplar seems to anchor tokenization boundaries for CSV outputs.

Observed failure modes (notes from initial 40-doc run):
- rdlw-7b-fp16 @ temp 0.2 often appended an extra comma ("entity,role,") causing csv parsers to fail. Suspect trailing-prompt whitespace/punctuation cue.
- rdlw-13b-q4 hallucinated dates when input had relative references ("last Tuesday"): model filled absolute dates ~2024-11-xx. Must add: "Do not convert relative dates to absolute."
- At temp 0.7, even with FORMAT:JSONL, models created nested objects ("attributes": {..}) which downstream pipeline doesn't accept. Fix: require "flat keys only" in constraint.

Mini experiments (examples I ran):
- Prompt A (minimal, no exemplar):
  "TASK: Extract fields
   FORMAT: CSV: org,role
   CONSTRAINT: Only use the text below.
   TEXT: [doc]"
  -> rdlw-7b: 82% compliance, but 12% trailing commas.
- Prompt B (add 1-shot single line exemplar):
  "TASK: Extract fields
   FORMAT: CSV: org,role
   EXEMPLAR:
   Input: 'Acme Inc. appointed Jane Doe as CFO'
   Output: 'Acme Inc.,CFO'
   CONSTRAINT: Only use the text below.
   TEXT: [doc]"
  -> rdlw-7b: 93% compliance, trailing commas down to 3%.

Failure-case bank (for later uploads to prompt-regressions):
- tokenization-split-entity: entity with punctuation ("ACME, Ltd") becomes two fields.
- trailing-comma: model reliably adds trailing comma when exemplar ends with a comma in examples.
- nested-structure: model invents nested keys despite "flat" instruction after longer contexts.
- relative-date-resolve: model replaces "yesterday" with an absolute date (bad).

Quick mitigations I've tried:
- Add explicit parser-clean hints: "Do not add extra delimiter at end."
- Put exemplar and format on same line to reduce ambiguous line breaks.
- Use post-token filter (regex) that removes trailing commas and verifies column count.

Open Qs / next steps:
- How small can exemplar be and still provide the anchor? Try micro-exemplar = 6 tokens vs 20 tokens.
- Re-run across rdlw-7b/13b/70b with the same random seed and track stable failure set.
- Explore tiny suffix token that prevents trailing comma (e.g. append "END" token after expected output).

To-dos (personal):
- [ ] Create small harness (python) to compute structure_compliance automatically and upload results to GH PR linked above.
- [ ] Add 100 edge-case docs focused on punctuation and relative dates.
- [ ] Submit brief notes to MLINF-342 with failure-case summaries.

Slack/refs:
- Quick convo: #applied-ml prompt-canon thread -> ping @ethank for exemplar format idea.
- Related PR: github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-canon/pull/67 (local harness and metrics).

One-line conclusions so far:
- Short, concrete FORMAT lines + a one-line exemplar drastically reduce format drift for short outputs.
- Add targeted constraint lines for common hallucination types (dates, nesting).

Random scratch ideas (brain dump):
- Microcanon registry: small YAML of primitives that engineers can pick/compose (simple UI in Console later).
- On-model tokenizer-aware exemplar generator: auto produce an exemplar that avoids tokenizer splits on commas/slashes.
- Tiny output-prover: lightweight regex checks returned inline feedback to model (two-pass minimal correction).

End of page. 
(Notes intentionally sparse — this is a private personal tracker before formalizing into prompt-canon PR.)
